label: Mark van Roojen, Moral Cognitivism vs §4.1…: Blackburn's logic of attitudes: a moral conditional…
locator: §4.1, 4.1.1 A logic of attitudes, 'Conditionals express higher order attitudes towards accepting certain conjunctions of attitudes.'
interpretation: Blackburn (1984, 195, quoted in the entry): 'If lying is wrong, telling your little brother to lie is wrong' expresses approval of making disapproval of getting one's brother to lie follow upon disapproval of lying; whoever holds that attitude and disapproves of lying but not of getting little brother to lie has a 'fractured sensibility'. Validity is explained by the irrationality of that constellation of attitudes. Blackburn's variant of the theory; it presupposes constant meaning for the embedded sentence ('the judgements that would be expressed by the sentences which they embed'). Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
